channel.title: Artificial Intelligence
channel.description: Official Machine Learning Blog of Amazon Web Services

item.title: How MoEngage built agentic customer engagement on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: MoEngage built Merlin AI, a set of AI agents on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that let marketing and product teams draft, analyze, and adjust campaigns from a single conversation. Learn how MoEngage turned its existing APIs into MCP tools and kept each tenant's data isolated while giving agents secure access to live platform data.

item.title: Modernizing mainframe Assembler to Java using Amazon Bedrock and AWS Transform
item.description: Legacy mainframe Assembler applications are costly to maintain and hard to staff. This post presents a multi-stage, AI-powered methodology using Amazon Bedrock, Kiro IDE, and AWS Transform to extract business rules, convert Assembler through an intermediate COBOL stage, and deploy modernized Java Spring Boot applications on AWS.

item.title: Novo Nordisk modernizes manufacturing process documents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: Novo Nordisk's Manufacturing Technology team within the Tablet area team built a process-intelligence assistant on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using a GraphRAG architecture that pairs a knowledge graph in Amazon Neptune with hybrid search in Amazon OpenSearch Serverless to turn millions of controlled manufacturing documents into grounded, cited answers.

item.title: Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
item.description: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports tabular search, so agentic retrieval can answer questions over CSV, XLSX, and XLS files. It looks up values and runs calculations across every relevant row, then combines the results with facts from related documents to answer multi-step analytical questions.

item.title: Best practices for writing Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
item.description: With Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, you block a content category by describing it in plain language, and the guardrail matches by meaning rather than keyword, which can block more than you intend. This post presents eight best practices for writing a topic precisely enough that the guardrail blocks what you mean and passes what you don't.

item.title: Customize answers per tenant in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
item.description: Retrieval instructions in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base set the voice, format, retrieval guidance, and answer policy for each tenant on shared knowledge bases. This post shows how to give each tenant its own answers, keep tenant data apart with metadata filters, scope access with IAM tags, and roll out changes one tenant at a time.

item.title: Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Many generative AI applications resend the same long context on every request. Prompt caching lets open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock reuse it to reduce input cost and latency. This post shows implicit and explicit caching through the Chat Completions API and applies caching to an OpenCode coding agent session.

item.title: Production MLOps at GS Caltex with Amazon SageMaker Canvas, part 1
item.description: GS Caltex connects Amazon SageMaker Canvas to Amazon SageMaker Pipelines so process engineers' no-code models run in production. This post shows how ML engineers reuse validated preprocessing flows and models, cutting deployment from about a week to a few hours and running batch inference every 30 minutes.

item.title: Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard
item.description: Coding agents work in tasks, and the number that matters is cost per solved task, not price per token. In this post, you use the AWS CDK to deploy LiteLLM with the NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard routing plugin on Amazon Bedrock, then measure cost per solved task for a routed model group against single-model baselines.

item.title: Architecture patterns for fast session startup on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime
item.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime V2 snapshots your initialized environment and restores it for each new session, so session start no longer grows with image size. This post explains how V2 starts a session, how to measure session start time, and four patterns to keep work off the first request.

item.title: OpenFold3 on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart: Predict biomolecular structures
item.description: Deploy OpenFold3-preview from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart to predict 3D structures of proteins, DNA, RNA, and ligand complexes in your own AWS account. The post covers asynchronous inference, multi-GPU parallelism, bringing your own MSAs for accuracy and privacy, and scaling to zero to reduce cost.

item.title: Cost-optimizing AssemblyAI speech-to-text inference on AWS with Amazon EC2 Spot
item.description: Learn how AssemblyAI runs cost-optimized speech-to-text inference at scale on AWS, using Amazon ECS, Amazon EC2 Spot GPU instances, and an Amazon SQS-based retry architecture to achieve 70% cost savings while maintaining SLA commitments across European Regions.

item.title: Cost attribution and controls for AI developer and productivity tools on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Amazon Bedrock provides built-in, zero-instrumentation cost attribution that traces every inference call back to the IAM principal that made it. This post shows how to attribute per-user Bedrock costs for AI developer and productivity tools using IAM Identity Center, session tags, and CUR 2.0, and how to enforce per-user usage limits.

item.title: Build a model improvement flywheel with Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture
item.description: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Data Capture records live inference inputs and outputs to Amazon S3. This post walks through one end-to-end example: capturing a support router's production traffic, surfacing a new-product blind spot with Amazon Athena, fine-tuning on the captured data with the HyperPod training operator, and measuring the before-and-after lift.

item.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron
item.description: SGLang-Neuron is now publicly available through an AWS Deep Learning Container. With SGLang-Neuron, you can serve models and generate reinforcement learning rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface you already know, all running on native PyTorch.

item.title: How Natera designed an agentic AI system for lab ops with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: Natera built SWARM, an agentic AI system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that captures institutional lab-operations knowledge and deploys it at scale. This post walks through the full architecture, from knowledge base construction to deployment and evaluation, delivering about 130x faster first response and 96.2% automated coverage across support tickets.

item.title: Four Amazon Bedrock inference choices that affect cost
item.description: Your Amazon Bedrock inference bill can keep climbing even after you tune prompts and application logic. Four request-level choices (cache duration, service tier, reasoning effort, and maxTokens) change how many tokens the service processes and the rate applied. We show how we tested each and how to verify the effect.

item.title: Tokenomics at scale: Track and cap Amazon Bedrock spend per IAM principal with CUR 2.0 and AWS Budgets
item.description: Get per-identity Amazon Bedrock cost visibility and enforceable spend limits using only AWS-native features, with no application code for the common case. Attribute spend with IAM principal tags, report with CUR 2.0 or Cost Explorer, and enforce with AWS Budgets actions that apply a Deny policy when a threshold is crossed.

item.title: Optimizing cost per task and proving agent ROI on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Comparing per-token prices hides the real cost of running a model on Amazon Bedrock. This post shows how to calculate the true cost per task across four hidden cost drivers, reduce it with caching, routing, and output constraints, and prove agent ROI with human baselines, holdout experiments, and a five-dimension scorecard.

item.title: Building a self-service LLM gateway with Amazon Bedrock and LiteLLM
item.description: Build a self-service LLM gateway with LiteLLM on AWS Fargate that puts Amazon Bedrock foundation models behind an OpenAI-compatible API. Developers get instant access through a single API key, while platform teams gain per-user cost controls, quota isolation, and observability.
